stem: A client asks how an excisional biopsy differs from a core needle biopsy. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: An excisional biopsy surgically removes the entire lump or suspicious area for pathologic examination, whereas a core needle biopsy removes a tissue sample with a wide needle.
options.B: An excisional biopsy and a core needle biopsy both remove only a small portion of the lesion, but they use different anesthetic medications.
options.C: A core needle biopsy removes the entire suspicious lesion, whereas an excisional biopsy removes only a narrow tissue cylinder.
options.D: An excisional biopsy establishes that no further cancer surgery can ever be needed because removal of the visible lesion is always definitive treatment.

rationale: A is correct. NCI defines excisional biopsy as surgical removal of an entire lump or suspicious area for pathologic examination; a small amount of surrounding normal tissue may also be removed. NCI defines needle biopsy as removal of tissue or fluid with a needle and specifies that use of a wide needle is called a core biopsy. B is incorrect because excisional biopsy removes the whole suspicious area rather than merely a small sample. C reverses the procedures. D is incorrect because the definition of excisional biopsy does not establish that diagnostic removal is always definitive cancer treatment; subsequent management depends on the pathology and clinical context.
educational_objective: Differentiate excisional biopsy from core needle biopsy by the amount and method of tissue obtained, and avoid equating diagnostic excision with guaranteed definitive cancer treatment.
